Here you set the travel time to them and the teachers the school shares with them, and the schools borrow each other's rooms at fixed times. The other school sees only its own name, its rooms, the answers to loans and whether it shares a teacher with the school: no pupils, timetables or people.

requirements.hoursCaveat: Hours count the academic year's calendar weeks and deduct holidays and staff days: a whole break week disappears, a single staff day takes a fifth of its week. It is an estimate at requirement level — a requirement says how many lessons a week, never on which weekdays, so nothing can know whether the staff day fell on one of this subject's lesson days. Right averaged over a term, wrong for any single week.

blocks.warnOne: A block needs at least two entries for anything to be placed together.
blocks.warnTeacher: {first} and {second} have the same teacher, who cannot teach both at once. The generator refuses the block.
blocks.warnGroup: {first} and {second} are the same group, and the same pupils cannot be in both at once. The generator refuses the block.
blocks.warnSplit: {first} and {second} both have their lessons split between teachers, and the lessons of a block are placed together one by one. The generator refuses the block. Give one of them one teacher again, or take it out of the block.
blocks.memberNotice: The entry is in a parallel block, and its lessons and weeks are the whole block's. Change the whole block's lessons with Change lessons under Blocks, or take the entry out of the block to change them here alone.
blocks.memberNoticeLinked: The entry is in the block {block}, which is placed at the same times as the block {other}, and the entries of both blocks have the same lessons. Change them with Change lessons under Blocks, which changes both blocks at once. Each block's weeks are its own. Do not take the entry out of the block to change its lessons here alone: it would then no longer be placed at the same times as the block {other}.
blocks.lessonsNamed: Change the lessons of the block {name}
blocks.lessonsDescription: {count, plural, one {The block's entry gets} other {The block's # entries get}} these lessons at once, so they are still placed at the same times. Each entry's teachers are checked against the staffing as when an entry is changed.
blocks.lessonsSaved: The lessons of the block {name} were saved.

termHalves.title: Split {post} into half classes
termHalves.description: The class is split into two halves that take turns over two periods, whole terms or half terms. With one subject each half takes it in its own period. With two subjects the halves take one each at the same time and swap in the second period. Each new entry gets the same changing time and weeks as {post}, and counts for the teacher and co-teacher at the same percentages ({teacherPercent} % and {coTeacherPercent} %).
termHalves.noSubjects: The school has no subject called textiles or wood and metalwork. The halves swap between two subjects, because a group has one entry per subject. Add the subjects under Subjects first and give them the same national code as {subject}, or choose two other subjects here.
termHalves.oneHalf: {group} only has the half {half}. Remove it under Classes and try again, and the class is split into two new halves.

preset.yearHalves: First and second half of the academic year
preset.autumnHalves: First and second half of the autumn
preset.springHalves: First and second half of the spring
preset.firstHalves: First half of the autumn and first half of the spring

periodsInvalid.MISSING: Give the first and last day of both periods.
periodsInvalid.BACKWARDS: A period does not end before it starts.
periodsInvalid.OUTSIDE_YEAR: Both periods lie within the academic year.

termHalves.periodsNotDrawn: The term is too short to split into two halves. Choose another day or Own dates.

termHalves.coTeacherCarriedOne: The class's entry has the co-teacher {name}. They follow both halves' entries unless you choose otherwise.
termHalves.coTeacherInactive: The class's entry has a co-teacher who is not among the school's active teachers. They do not follow to the new entries.
termHalves.teachersSame: The halves have lessons at the same time, so the same person cannot be teacher or co-teacher in both subjects. Choose different people.
termHalves.springStartHint: The autumn entries run until the day before, the spring ones from this day.
termHalves.springStartHalvesHint: The terms are split here, and each term into two halves with as many teaching weeks once holidays and staff days are taken off. Choose Own dates to change a period.
termHalves.springOutside: Choose a day after the first day of the academic year and no later than its last.

termHalves.lessonsOwn: The halves take {lessons} a week in their period. The class's entry has {classLessons}.
termHalves.lessonsUseClass: The pace of the class's entry
termHalves.lessonsInvalid: 1 to 40 lessons a week, of 15 to 240 minutes in steps of 5.

termHalves.hoursHalvesSubject: {first} gets {firstHours} of {subject} and {second} {secondHours} over the academic year. The class's entry gives each pupil {classHours}.

timplan.failed: The curriculum could not be read, so the halves' minutes are not compared with the targets.
timplan.noGrade: {group} has no year, so the halves' minutes are not compared with a curriculum.
timplan.noPlan: Year {grade} follows no curriculum this academic year, so the halves' minutes are not compared with a target.
timplan.double: {subject} reaches each pupil both from {group} and from the half. The coverage page therefore says the pupils are double planned in {subject}.
timplan.reduction: With the swap each pupil gets more {subject} than the target of {target}. {post} can go from {from} to {to} a week with no half under the target: {first} then gets {firstPlanned} and {second} {secondPlanned}.
timplan.reductionApply: Change {post} to {to} when the class is split
timplan.reductionUnplaced: Until the halves hold at least half of the class's pupils, Target mode and the coverage page show {subject} for {group} as {planned} of {target}, under the target, since the class is then judged on its own entries.
timplan.reductionInBlock: {post} is in a parallel block, so its lessons are changed with Change lessons under Blocks.

termHalves.halvesExist: The class's halves {first} and {second} are used.
termHalves.blockNamesInvalid: The blocks need two different names.

termHalves.replacesOne: {post} is removed and replaced by two entries, one for each half in its period. Each entry gets a block of its own.

termHalves.codeDiffers: {subject} does not have the same national code as {post} ({code}). Create curriculum entries will then not see that the halves take the class's {post}, and the curriculum's national rows will not count {subject} as {code}.
termHalves.codeMissingOnPost: {post} has no national code, so Create curriculum entries will not see that the halves' {subject} is taken instead of the class's {post}. Give the subjects the same national code.
termHalves.codeSwapOwn: {subject} has another national code than {post}. In the swap, the halves' minutes in {subject} count on its own code ({code}), together with the class's own entries there, as the rows against the curriculum show.
termHalves.codeSwapMissing: {subject} has no national code. The dialog then counts it as a subject of its own beside {post}, and the curriculum's national rows count the halves' minutes in it as the school's own choice. Give the subject a code under Subjects: the same as {post}'s if the halves take {post} in it, and the class's pace is enough.
termHalves.generatorNote: The second period's block takes the first period's times, so the halves have their lessons at the same times all year: generation gives each entry of the second period the times and room the first period's entry in its subject got. Lock one block with Lock block, or drag its card, in the master timetable and the other follows (see the manual, 4.2).
termHalves.generatorNoteOne: Generation places the first half's {subject} and keeps the times free for the whole class. The second half's {subject} is written at the same times and in the same room in its period. Generation plans one week, so the times are kept free all year, outside the periods too. In the master timetable each half's lesson is a block card of its own: Lock block locks both halves' lessons, and dragging one half's card takes the other half's lesson with it. Change the halves' lessons with Change lessons under Blocks, which changes both (see the manual, 4.2).
termHalves.sharesRefused: {post} splits its lessons between teachers. Remove the split in the entry's dialog first, then choose a teacher for each subject here.

timplan.title: Timplan
timplan.subtitle: The school's local timplan: minutes per week in every subject and year, set against the Education Ordinance's hours per stage
timplan.noPlansBody: Create the school's timplan here: a draft in minutes per week and year that shows, stage by stage, how it compares with the national timplan.
timplan.loadFailed: The timplan could not be loaded
timplan.loadFailedHint: Try again in a moment. Nothing shown here has changed.
timplan.weeksHint: Suggested: 35.6 weeks — 178 school days divided by 5. Minutes per week times the weeks, divided by 60, gives the stage's hours.
timplan.weeksInvalid: Enter 20.0–40.0 weeks with at most one decimal.

tones.below: below target, within the school's choice

timplan.legend: Green meets the target. Amber is below the target but within what the school's choice may take. Red is below the target where the ordinance does not allow it: a protected subject, more than the cap, or a science or social studies subject under its minimum.
timplan.notCountedHeading: Does not count as teaching time
timplan.notCountedHint: Mentor time, resource time and the like. The minutes are saved but join no total.
timplan.skolansValBadgeHint: No national subject code: the minutes count as the school's choice.
timplan.ownTimeBadgeHint: No national subject code, and this timplan has no school's-choice pool: the minutes count as the school's own time.
timplan.uncodedBadgeHint: The subject has no national subject code and no minutes yet that count toward the timplan. With a code it is compared with the national timplan.
timplan.uncodedNotice: {count, plural, one {One subject that counts as teaching time has no national subject code, so its minutes} other {# subjects that count as teaching time have no national subject code, so their minutes}} count toward no subject in the national timplan.
timplan.outsideStagesHint: The preschool class and years the school form does not have belong to no stage. The minutes are saved but do not count toward the timplan.
timplan.noSubjects: The school has no subjects yet. Add them under Subjects first.
timplan.footerColumnSumAlternatives: Swedish/Swedish as a second language and language choice count once per year, at the longest alternative: a pupil takes one of them.
timplan.footerSkolansValValue: {taken} of {available} h taken from subjects · {placed} h placed in own subjects and above targets
timplan.footerSkolansValNone: No pool to compare with in this timplan · {placed} h placed
timplan.footerSkolansValEmpty: Nothing planned yet that counts toward the timplan.
timplan.footerSkolansValUnpublished: The distribution is not published, so there are no subjects to take from or place above.
timplan.unpublishedBody: The distribution between subjects and stages for {version} has not been published yet. The plan is only compared with the guaranteed total of {total} h — not subject by subject.
timplan.warningsEmpty: The plan meets the national timplan in every subject and stage.
timplan.warningsHint: Click a row to highlight the cells it is about. Nothing here stops the plan from being saved or decided.
timplan.warningsLive: Computed from what you typed — not saved yet.

timplan.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Save or discard before switching plan, deciding or importing.
timplan.invalidCells: {count, plural, one {# cell has} other {# cells have}} a value that is not 0–1200 whole minutes.
timplan.decidedReadOnly: A decided timplan does not change. Reopen it to keep working in a new draft; the decided one stays as it is.

timplan.decisionNotePlaceholder: Decided by the governing body 2026-05-12, ref …

timplan.copyNameHint: Left empty, the draft is named {name}.
timplan.reopened: A new draft has been created.
timplan.deleteBodyDraft: The draft and all its cells are deleted. This cannot be undone.

timplan.noVersionForForm: There is no national timplan for that school form.
timplan.importInto: The cells are read into the draft {name}.

timplan.importNotDraft: A decided timplan does not take a file. Reopen it as a draft first.

yearTimplans.title: Timplan per year
yearTimplans.body: Which local timplan each year group follows during the academic year. A new academic year follows the most recently decided plan the cohort may follow; change it here. A draft may be chosen while next year is planned ahead of the decision, and is then marked as a draft wherever the targets are shown.
yearTimplans.cohortNote: A plan under the 2028 wording (7,424 hours in grundskolan) applies only to cohorts starting grade 1 in autumn 2028 or later; everyone already in school, the 2027/28 preschool class included, follows an older wording and keeps the older total (6,890 hours in grundskolan).
yearTimplans.yearLocked: Save or cancel before switching academic year.
yearTimplans.noYear: The school has no academic year yet. Create it under School setup first.
yearTimplans.loadFailed: The academic year's timplans could not be loaded. Close the dialog and try again.
yearTimplans.noPlans: The school has no local timplan yet.
yearTimplans.caption: Timplan per year group for {year}
yearTimplans.saved: Timplan per year group saved for {year}.

generate.title: Create curriculum entries
generate.body: Creates the curriculum entries the academic year's classes are missing according to {plan}: one entry per class and subject the plan gives time in the class's year group. Existing entries are never changed, teaching groups are not created and no teacher is set — do that afterwards under Curriculum entries. Modern languages are never put on a class, and of Swedish and Swedish as a second language a class gets only one.
generate.noYears: The school has no academic year yet.
generate.lengthHintCommon: The suggestion {minutes} is the length the year's entries use most.
generate.lengthHintDefault: The year has no entries yet, so the suggestion is {minutes} minutes.
generate.splitLabel: Split the remainder so the target is met without surplus
generate.splitHint: The target is met without surplus where possible: 175 minutes at 60 becomes 2 × 60 + 1 × 55, and 120 at 80 becomes 1 × 80 + 1 × 40. Beside two or more lessons, a remainder of at most half the length is added to one of them instead, so 200 at 60 becomes 1 × 80 + 2 × 60.
generate.roundUpHint: Whole lessons, rounded up: 175 minutes at 60 becomes 3 × 60, 5 above target.
generate.splitNote: {count, plural, one {# entry gets} other {# entries get}} lengths other than whole lessons of the chosen length, so the target is met without surplus. Make uniform gives whole lessons instead.
generate.surplusHintSplit: The remainder becomes a lesson of its own or is added to another, so the entry meets the target; a small difference can remain where the timetable's 5-minute steps or 15-minute minimum length require it.

length.integer: Enter the lesson length in whole minutes.
length.range: The lesson length must be 15–240 minutes.
length.grid: The lesson length must be divisible by 5 — the scheduler counts in 5-minute steps.

generate.draft: The plan is a draft — not decided. The entries are created anyway and can be changed under Curriculum entries.
generate.noGrades: No year group follows {plan} in {year}, so there is nothing to create. Choose the plan under Timplan per year first.
generate.nothingToCreate: Nothing to create: {skipped, plural, one {# pair is skipped} other {# pairs are skipped}} — the classes already have the entries, or the subjects are taught in groups.

generate.skippedTitle: {count, plural, one {# pair is skipped} other {# pairs are skipped}}
generate.alternativesNote: Modern languages and Swedish as a second language are taught in teaching groups and are not created on the classes; create the groups under Groups and their entries under Curriculum entries.

generate.skippedAlternative: {group} · {subject} — alternative to {other}, taught in a group for the pupils who read it

generate.surplusHint: The number of lessons is rounded up so the entry reaches the target; the difference is shown in minutes per week, e.g. 175 min as 3 × 60 = +5.
generate.invalidRows: Some rows hold a value that cannot be saved: 1–40 lessons and 15–240 minutes in steps of 5.

generate.resultSkipped: {count, plural, one {# pair already existed and was left untouched.} other {# pairs already existed and were left untouched.}}
generate.resultNext: Set teachers and adjust entries under Curriculum entries.
generate.resultBlocks: The language-choice entries are in {blocks} and are placed at the same times when the timetable is generated.
generate.languagesHint: Choose the teaching groups that read each language, one or more, for example 7sp1, 7sp2 and 7sp3 for Spanish in year 7. Each group gets an entry, and all language-choice entries of a year are posted in one block, Språkval åk 7, so the language choice takes one slot of the class's week per lesson. A group can be chosen for one language only. A language without a group is not created.

constraints.title: Availability
constraints.subtitle: When teachers, rooms or classes are unavailable
constraints.empty: No constraints. The AI engine will treat every resource as always available.
constraints.preferencesHint: State what should preferably happen, as opposed to the absolute rules above. The engine tries to honour these but will break a wish rather than make the week unschedulable.
constraints.preferenceWeightHint: How much the engine may give up elsewhere to honour the wish. The scale is the one the optimization profile uses: 5 weighs the same as the other preferences, above 10 the wish starts overriding goals such as spreading subjects across the week.
constraints.gradeHint: The rule applies to every class and teaching group with students in the range.
constraints.locksHint: A lock is absolute: the subject's lessons may only be in the rooms you choose. If it cannot be honoured the timetable is refused, naming the rule that is impossible — unlike the wishes below, which the solver weighs against everything else.
constraints.locksEmpty: No locks. Every room is allowed for every subject.
constraints.ruleGradesHint: The rule applies to a group whose years all fit inside the span. A group spanning 6-7 is therefore not reached by a rule for 7-9.
constraints.tableCaption: Constraints: what they apply to, when and why
constraints.loadFailed: The constraints could not be fetched
constraints.loadFailedHint: No list is shown, because an empty one would mean everyone is always available. Nothing has changed. Reload the page to try again.
constraints.dialogDescription: When a teacher, a room, a class or some years are unavailable, every week or on one date.
constraints.roomRulesLoadFailed: The room rules could not be fetched
constraints.roomRulesLoadFailedHint: No list is shown, because an empty one would mean there are no rules. Nothing has changed. Reload the page to try again.

constraints.deletePreferenceBody: {rule} is removed and is not weighed the next time a timetable is generated. Timetables already generated do not change.

frameTimes.title: Frame times
frameTimes.subtitle: The hours each stage may be timetabled within
frameTimes.empty: The whole school day is open to every year.

frameTimes.overlapHint: Frame times reaching the same group all apply at once, so the narrowest window wins. Writing “08:00–15:00 every day” and “08:00–13:00 Friday” makes Friday 08:00–13:00 with nothing to remove.
frameTimes.effectiveHint: Computed from the rows above, one stage per row.
frameTimes.duplicate: A frame time already exists for those years on that day.
frameTimes.changeoverHint: Time a class or teacher needs to move. The solver leaves at least this much between two consecutive lessons. 0 means no margin. Several matching frames give the largest — a frame is a bound, a margin is a floor.
frameTimes.offerWholeSchool: Add a frame for the whole school
frameTimes.loadFailed: The frame times could not be fetched
frameTimes.loadFailedHint: No list and no week are shown, because an empty list would mean the whole day is open. Nothing has changed. Reload the page to try again.
frameTimes.tableCaption: Frame times entered: years, day and time
frameTimes.dialogDescription: The hours these years may have lessons, every day or on one weekday.
frameTimes.deleteBody: {row} is removed. If no other frame time covers these years that day, the whole day opens for lessons.

breaks.title: Holidays and staff days
breaks.intro: The days the academic year has but the timetable does not. They are deducted from the curriculum's hours, and saving one removes any published lessons inside it from the calendar.
breaks.namePlaceholder: Autumn half term, Staff day, Work experience year 9…
breaks.datesHint: Both days are included. A single staff day has the same date in both fields.
breaks.gradeHint: The break applies to every class with students in the span. Teaching groups without a year of their own are not affected — their lessons stay and remain visible in the calendar.
breaks.deletesWarning: Saving removes published lessons inside the period from the calendar. Lessons that have already happened, been cancelled, or had attendance recorded are left alone. Shortening or deleting the break does not bring back lessons that were already removed.

breaks.empty: The curriculum's hours then count every calendar week as taught, which runs roughly 8–10 weeks high across a Swedish academic year.
breaks.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.

staffing.footGroupLosses: Every lost lesson counts once, in the pupils' lesson minutes and not per teacher.
staffing.footDefinition: Delivered is lessons that were held, are not cancelled and have at least one teacher — the same definition of held time as Timplan › Coverage, but with every subject, including those that do not count toward the timplan: a teacher's mentor time is teaching too.
staffing.footCredit: A held lesson is credited to the teacher rows on it: the lead and the co-teacher at the row's percentage, a substitute at 100 %. A lead or co-teacher left beside a substitute is credited to nobody.
staffing.footCoTeacher: Covered by others reads the master schedule's current teacher and co-teacher, not whoever was scheduled that day. A substitute replaces every teacher row on the lesson, so a co-teacher who was there counts here and not as delivered.
staffing.footScheduled: Scheduled is today's master schedule counted over the period; changes during the period show in Delivered. Parked lessons do not count as scheduled but count as delivered if they were held.
staffing.footGrade: Planned is counted per school day in the period, holidays by the group's own grade, as publishing does. The weekly report under Staffing counts a standard week.
staffing.footAhead: Upcoming: lessons in the period that have not ended yet. Cancelled upcoming lessons count as neither lost nor upcoming. Holidays and staff days are not a loss.
staffing.footRounding: Each row, each teacher's total and the totals are rounded on their own (rounded per row): a teacher's total is not always the sum of the rows under it.
staffing.footFactor: Model Factor: the minutes are counted time, lesson time × the subject's factor. The factor is the school's per subject and applies to every school year; changing it changes earlier years' figures too.

schedule.title: Nightly sync
schedule.body: A scheduled sync reads the register every night. Its diff waits for your review just as when you sync by hand, unless you also turn on automatic apply below.
schedule.hourHint: The sync runs at or after the hour, once a night, also when daylight saving time begins or ends.
schedule.fullEveryDaysHint: 1–31. Other nights read only what changed. A change you leave out comes back at the next full sync.
schedule.autoApplyBody: Only what is safe is applied at night; the rest waits for you.
schedule.autoApplyNeedsSchedule: Turn on the nightly sync first.
schedule.autoApplyDoes: Applied automatically: names, class moves, new teaching-group memberships, guardian links between people already linked who have no protected identity, duties, and deactivating pupils and guardians.
schedule.autoApplyNever: Never automatically: new people, links, email changes, reactivations, deactivating staff, anything you changed yourself since the last sync, and anything about a person with a protected identity.
schedule.autoApplyBrake: More than 5 deactivations, or more than 2 % of the linked people if that is higher, stop the night entirely.

sync.title: Sync
sync.body: A sync reads the register and shows what would change. Nothing changes until you have reviewed and applied the diff. Nothing is deleted: whoever left the register is deactivated.

codes.SS12000_APPLY_FAILED: The changes could not be applied; nothing was saved.
codes.SS12000_ADDRESS_REFUSED: The address points to an internal or private network, which Rastra timetable does not connect to.
codes.SS12000_CONNECTION_FAILED: Could not connect to the register.
codes.SS12000_DNS_FAILED: The register's host name could not be resolved.
codes.SS12000_TLS_FAILED: The TLS handshake failed: the certificate was not accepted, or the client certificate is missing or was refused.
codes.SS12000_TIMEOUT: The register did not answer within 30 seconds.
codes.SS12000_REDIRECT_REFUSED: The register answered with a redirect, and Rastra timetable follows none. Check the address.
codes.SS12000_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE: An answer from the register was larger than 32 MB.
codes.SS12000_NOT_JSON: The register did not answer with JSON. Check that the address ends in /v2.0.
codes.SS12000_INVALID_JSON: The register answered with broken JSON.
codes.SS12000_INVALID_RESPONSE: The register's answer did not have the shape SS12000 2.1 prescribes.
codes.SS12000_ORGANISATION_INVALID: An organisation in the register did not have the shape SS12000 2.1 prescribes.
codes.SS12000_PAGE_LOOP: The register did not stop paging (too many pages, or the same page again).
codes.SS12000_RATE_LIMITED: The register limited the requests even after three attempts.
codes.SS12000_UNAUTHORIZED: The register did not accept the sign-in (401).
codes.SS12000_FORBIDDEN: The register refused access (403). The client probably lacks permission for this data.
codes.SS12000_TOKEN_REFUSED: The token service refused the client id or client secret.
codes.SS12000_SECRET_MISSING: A credential is missing. Enter it under Credentials.
codes.SS12000_SECRET_UNREADABLE: A saved credential can no longer be read, for example after the address changed. Enter it again.
codes.SS12000_SECRETS_NOT_CONFIGURED: The server lacks the key that encrypts secrets (INTEGRATION_SECRETS_KEY). Contact operations.
codes.SS12000_SOURCE_EMPTY: The register answered with no pupils or no staff although linked people exist. No diff was made; check the client's permissions at the register.
codes.SS12000_DEPENDENCY_NOT_APPLIED: Skipped: the change it depends on was not chosen.
codes.SS12000_TARGET_CHANGED: Skipped: the row had changed in Rastra timetable.
codes.SS12000_HALF_MEMBER_NOT_IN_CLASS: Skipped: the pupil is not in the class of the half, or is already in the class's other half.
codes.STALE: The run was interrupted (the server restarted) and marked as failed.
codes.EXPIRED: The diff was not reviewed within 30 days and was discarded.
codes.REVIEW_PENDING: The nightly sync was skipped because a manual diff is waiting for review.
codes.INVALID_RECORD: A record in the register had the wrong shape and was not read.
codes.PERSON_RECORD_INVALID: The register sent this person, but the record had the wrong shape. They are not deactivated for it; fix the record in the register.
codes.ROSTER_HAS_INVALID_RECORDS: A record in the register could not be read, so the absence may come from it. The deactivation happens only if you choose it.
codes.SS12000_LOOKUP_REFUSED: The register refused to look people up; guardians and others only named were not read.
codes.PERSON_NOT_YET_ENROLLED: The pupil starts later and is added when the enrolment begins.
codes.DELETED_BUT_RETURNED: The register both deleted and sent the record in the same run; it is kept.
codes.PERSON_ROLE_MISMATCH: The role in the register differs from the role in Rastra timetable. A sync never changes a role.
codes.PERSON_DEACTIVATED_LOCALLY: An administrator deactivated this person in Rastra timetable, and a sync does not reactivate them.
codes.LOCAL_EDIT_SINCE_LAST_SYNC: Changed in Rastra timetable since the last sync; never applied automatically.
codes.PERSON_EMAIL_TAKEN: Somebody else in Rastra timetable already uses the email address.
codes.PERSON_EMAIL_CHANGE_INVITED: The person is already invited and signs in with the old address. Change it only if the sign-in should follow.
codes.PERSON_NO_EMAIL: The register has no usable email address for the person.
codes.PERSON_AMBIGUOUS_MATCH: The address fits several people, so nobody is linked automatically.
codes.PERSON_MATCHES_INACTIVE: The address belongs to a deactivated person. Link and reactivate only if it is the same human being.
codes.PERSON_ADMIN_UNTOUCHED: An administrator is linked but never changed by a sync.
codes.PERSON_MULTIPLE_ROLES: The person has several roles in the register; Rastra timetable gives each person one role.
codes.DUTY_ROLE_REVIEW: The duty would give a teacher sign-in with access to pupils' data. Choose it only if that is right.
codes.DUTY_NON_TEACHING_ROLE: The duty is not a teaching duty.
codes.GROUP_OUTSIDE_YEARS: The group lies outside the school's academic years.
codes.GROUP_SPANS_YEARS: The group spans several academic years and is linked to the one that applies today.
codes.GROUP_YEAR_CHANGED: The group belongs to a different academic year in the register than in Rastra timetable.
codes.GROUP_KIND_MISMATCH: A class in one system and a teaching group in the other.
codes.GROUP_NAME_TAKEN: Another group of the year already has the name.
codes.GROUP_DELETED_AT_SOURCE: The group was deleted in the register. It stays in Rastra timetable.
codes.MEMBERSHIP_MULTIPLE_CLASSES: The pupil is in several classes in the register.
codes.MEMBERSHIP_CLASS_NOT_LINKED: The class is not linked to Rastra timetable yet.
codes.MEMBERSHIP_ENDED_AT_SOURCE: The membership has ended in the register. A sync never removes it; remove it by hand if it should go.
codes.RESPONSIBLE_NOT_PROVISIONED: The guardian is not in Rastra timetable.
codes.RESPONSIBLE_ENDED_AT_SOURCE: The register no longer names the guardian for the child. A sync never removes the link.
codes.ORGANISATION_NAME_DIFFERS: The school unit has another name in the register. The school's name in Rastra timetable does not change.
codes.ORGANISATION_NOT_SKOLENHET: The organisation is not a school unit in the register and does not become one in Rastra timetable.
codes.SCHOOL_UNIT_TYPES_UNSUPPORTED: The register lists school types Rastra timetable does not hold; they are not written.
codes.SCHOOL_UNIT_CODE_INVALID: The register's school unit code is not eight digits and is not written.
codes.SCHOOL_UNIT_CODE_TAKEN: Another school unit in Rastra timetable already has that code.
codes.SCHOOL_UNIT_SPAN_OVERLAP: The grades would belong to two school units. Change the units' grades under Classes.
codes.SCHOOL_UNIT_NOT_CHOSEN: The school unit is linked but no longer chosen. It stays in Rastra timetable.
codes.GROUP_UNIT_MISMATCH: The class's grade puts it in another school unit than the register does. Change the units' grades or the class's grade.

signIn.domainsHint: Anyone who types an address on one of these domains may choose Sign in with school account. One domain per line, for example skola.se: domains the school's teachers and administrators have addresses on.
signIn.domainsInvalid: Write each domain without @ and without https, for example skola.se. At most 20.
signIn.domainsPersonal: Personal mail domains cannot sign in with a school account: {domains}. Staff with such an address need one in the organisation, from SS12000 or from whoever runs Rastra timetable, and their login has to move there with it. It moves only when you send the invitation again.
signIn.tenantHint: Found under Overview in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Only accounts from that organisation get in.
signIn.tenantInvalid: A tenant ID is a GUID: 32 characters in five groups separated by hyphens.
signIn.hostedDomainHint: The organisation's primary domain in Google Workspace. Only accounts from there get in.
signIn.hostedDomainInvalid: Write the domain without @ and without https, for example skola.se.
signIn.hostedDomainPersonal: A personal mail domain belongs to no Workspace. Write the organisation's domain, for example skola.se.
signIn.ssoOnlyBody: Teachers and administrators then cannot sign in with a password, and anyone signed in with a password is signed out within an hour. Pupils and guardians are not affected. Do not turn it on until staff have a version of the app with the Sign in with school account button: an older app then cannot sign in at all. A school-account sign-in lasts one day at a time.
signIn.ssoOnlyNeedsOwn: Sign in with a school account from this organisation first. That shows the sign-in works before anyone depends on it.
signIn.ssoOnlySaved: Staff now sign in with their school account.
signIn.ssoOnlyOff: Staff can sign in with a password again.
signIn.signedInWithAzure: You are signed in with a school account from Microsoft Entra ID.
signIn.signedInWithGoogle: You are signed in with a school account from Google Workspace.
signIn.signedInWithPassword: You are signed in with a password.
signIn.removeTitle: Turn off signing in with school account?
signIn.removeBody: Everyone signs in with a password again. Anyone signed in with a school account is signed out within an hour, and anyone who never chose a password uses Forgot your password?.
signIn.removed: Signing in with school account is turned off.
signIn.setupHint: Before staff can sign in, the organisation's IT administrator must approve Rastra timetable in Microsoft Entra ID or allow it in Google Workspace. Then try it yourself: sign out and choose Sign in with school account.

huvudmanKeys.title: {name}'s keys
huvudmanKeys.body: The owner's SS12000 keys read the school as the school's own keys do, attendance and absence aside. The owner's municipal administrator makes and revokes them; the school ends them all by leaving its owner, under Data protection.
huvudmanKeys.notDecider: The principal and full administrators see the huvudman's keys here and under Data protection.

csvImport.title: Import CSV
csvImport.kindLabel: What do you want to import?
csvImport.noActiveYear: No active academic year. Activate a year before importing.
csvImport.importingIntoYear: The rows will be imported into {year}.
csvImport.rowsReady: {count, plural, one {# row ready to import} other {# rows ready to import}}
csvImport.updatesNotDeletes: The import adds new rows and updates the ones already there. Rows you removed from the file are NOT removed from the curriculum, and a column the file does not have is left alone. But an EMPTY cell in a column the file does have clears that field — that is how you remove a teacher or a period. To remove a whole entry, click it in the table.

lunch.title: Lunch and dining hall
lunch.hint: The solver keeps a lunch break free for every class and staggers the sittings so the dining hall is never over-filled.
lunch.seatsHint: Left empty, the solver assumes everyone can eat at once.
lunch.maxPerDayHint: Applies per class and teaching group.
lunch.notDefined: Lunch has not been defined yet
lunch.rulesIntro: Hard rules for the whole school, which every generated timetable must keep.
lunch.loadFailed: The school rules could not be fetched
lunch.loadFailedHint: The form is not shown, because it would otherwise be filled with defaults that could be saved over the school's real rules. Reload the page to try again.
lunch.saveFailed: The school rules were not saved
lunch.saveFailedHint: The rules that applied before still stand.
lunch.travel: The generator keeps the travel time between sites
lunch.travelHint: A teacher, or the pupils, with two lessons on one day at different sites get the travel time between them, rounded up to whole start steps of the timetable. The travel times are set under Rooms, Sites.
lunch.pupilGaps: The generator keeps pupils' idle time down
lunch.pupilGapsHint: The gaps between a pupil's first and last lesson are counted per pupil, with the class, the teaching groups, the halves and the replacing groups, as on the Idle gaps page. A whole class waiting weighs twice what a teacher waiting does. A good timetable may take longer to find.

conflictCategories.TIMEOUT_PROBE: Rule that does not fit (measured, not proved)

gaps.title: Gaps and idle time
gaps.intro: Three questions asked of the base schedule: when are these free at the same time, where are the idle gaps, and who is free right then. All of it is computed in the browser from the schedule you already have — nothing is saved.
gaps.emptyHint: Generate or lay a schedule first, and there will be gaps to search.
gaps.freeHint: Pick the classes, teachers and rooms that must be free at the same time. The answer is the whole window, not every fifteen minutes — so you can see how much room you actually have to move into.
gaps.freeNobody: Pick at least one class, teacher or room — otherwise the question is about nobody.
gaps.freeNone: No shared free time of at least {minutes} for {who}. Try a shorter length or fewer of them.
gaps.freeCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 free window} other {# free windows}} for {who}
gaps.idleHint: An idle gap is a hole between the first and the last lesson of a day — time somebody spends waiting at school. It is counted per pupil, so a gap can be half a class while the other half is in a lesson. Time before the first and after the last lesson does not count; they are not here for it. Heaviest week first.
gaps.idleLunchWindow: {minutes} min of lunch is credited once a day, to the first gap in the window that can hold it.
gaps.idleLunchOff: No lunch break is configured, so no gap is credited for a meal.
gaps.idlePupilTime: The timetable plan gives some lessons extra time for the pupils — changing before and showering after. That time counts as occupied, so a gap that looks empty on the grid may be missing here: the class is in the changing room, and the timetable editor will not let a lesson in there either.
gaps.idleNone: No idle gaps of at least {minutes} anywhere in the schedule.
gaps.idleCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 class or teacher has idle gaps} other {# classes and teachers have idle gaps}}
gaps.idleSummary: Up to {total} idle in a single week, longest gap {worst}
gaps.idleStudents: {free} of {total, plural, =1 {1 pupil free} other {# pupils free}}
gaps.lengthLegend: Gaps are labelled by the waiting time left once lunch is subtracted — the same time the totals are counted in: under 40 minutes is short, 40–79 medium, 80 minutes and up long. A 1 h 40 min gap with 30 min of lunch therefore counts as 70 minutes: medium.
gaps.generatorFigure: The generator's number: {minutes, number} pupil-minutes of idle time in an ordinary week, {perPupil, number} minutes per pupil. It is counted as the list below is, with 15 minutes as the shortest gap, and each gap times the pupils sitting in it.
gaps.generatorFigureOn: Generate keeps it down when it lays a timetable (School rules).
gaps.generatorFigureOff: Generate does not take it into account until the school turns it on under School rules.
gaps.whoHint: Give a day and a time — the question you ask when you need a substitute on Wednesday at ten. Every class, teacher and room is tested on its own.
gaps.whoInvalid: The end time must be after the start time.
gaps.whoCount: {groups, plural, =1 {1 class} other {# classes}}, {teachers, plural, =1 {1 teacher} other {# teachers}} and {rooms, plural, =1 {1 room} other {# rooms}} are free {day} {start}–{end}
gaps.loadFailed: The timetable could not be loaded
gaps.loadFailedHint: The answers here are computed from the whole timetable, with the school’s rules and class lists. When part of it is missing, the page shows no answers rather than wrong ones. Nothing has changed. Reload the page.
gaps.noYearHint: The questions are asked of a school year’s base schedule. Create and activate the school year first; then there is a schedule to ask.

rasts.title: Breaks
rasts.subtitle: When each stage is not taught
rasts.hint: A break is minutes of the day a stage is free. The solver places no lessons across them, and they appear in the pupil's, guardian's and teacher's schedule. Several breaks a day is normal — every matching row applies.
rasts.name: Name
rasts.lessonBefore: Require a lesson before the break
rasts.lessonBeforeHint: The class must have at least one lesson between the previous break or lunch — or the start of the day — and this break, if it is still at school afterwards. Without it, a day may open with a break.
rasts.empty: Without them the solver places lessons back to back.
rasts.weekHint: The rows above read as a week. A day-specific break replaces only the every-day break whose time it overlaps — the others still stand that day.
rasts.deleteBody: {name} will be removed. The solver may then place lessons in that time on its next run.
rasts.loadFailed: The breaks could not be fetched
rasts.loadFailedHint: No list and no week are shown, because an empty list would mean the school has no breaks. Nothing has changed. Reload the page to try again.
rasts.dialogDescription: Minutes when these years are not taught, every day or on one weekday.

supervision.title: Break supervision
supervision.subtitle: Where the school supervises pupils during breaks, who is on duty when, and which breaks nobody covers. Shifts count as duties in teachers' load.
supervision.noYearTitle: The school has no school year
supervision.noYear: The supervision rota belongs to a school year. Add the year under School years first.
supervision.loadFailed: The supervision rota could not be loaded
supervision.loadFailedHint: No rota is shown, since an empty one would mean no break has anyone on duty. Nothing has changed; reload the page to try again.
supervision.peopleFailed: The teachers’ names could not be loaded, so the shifts are shown without them. Reload the page to try again.
supervision.noAreas: Add the places the school supervises, such as the playground, the dining hall and the corridor. Then you can put shifts on them.

gaps.title: Breaks without supervision
gaps.description: Breaks where fewer teachers are on duty than the area needs, at some minute of the break.
gaps.none: Every break has as many on duty as its area needs.
gaps.count: {count, plural, one {# break lacks supervision} other {# breaks lack supervision}}

grid.caption: Supervision rota for {area}: the breaks and who is on duty each weekday
grid.needs: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody required} one {Needs # on duty} other {Needs # on duty}}
grid.otherHint: Shifts outside every break of the area, such as the entrance before school or the bus after it.
grid.noBreaks: The area is supervised in no break: no year in its span has breaks or lunch it is supervised in. Shifts can still be put on it.

areas.title: Supervision areas
areas.description: The places the school supervises, and in which breaks. An area holds for every school year.
areas.caption: The school's supervision areas
areas.dialogHint: The breaks and lunch are read from Breaks and Lunch sittings for the years you set.
areas.name: Name
areas.gradesHint: The area is supervised during the breaks of these years.
areas.duringLunchHint: During the years' lunch sittings, or the school's lunch window where no sitting is set.
areas.guardsHint: With 0, no break is reported as uncovered.
areas.guardsInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to 10.
areas.nameTooLong: The name can be at most 60 characters.
areas.countsAsTeachingHint: Shifts count against the teaching target, as a duty that counts as teaching does. Organised break activities, for instance.
areas.saveFailed: The area could not be saved
areas.deleteBody: {count, plural, =0 {The area has no shifts.} one {# shift on the area is removed, in every school year.} other {# shifts on the area are removed, in every school year.}}

errors.SUPERVISION_AREA_NAME_TAKEN: The school already has a supervision area with that name.
errors.SUPERVISION_AREA_LIMIT: A school has at most 100 supervision areas.
errors.SUPERVISION_SITE_NOT_FOUND: The site no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.SUPERVISION_AREA_NOT_FOUND: The area no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_HAS_COVERS: The cover board has {count, plural, one {a decision} other {# decisions}} on break duties in this area from {date}. Undo {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} on the cover board first, so the substitute is told.

areas.nameHint: The name is unique across the school, sites included. Write Playground north, for instance.

shift.dialogHint: A shift is a teacher on an area on a weekday. Without dates it holds for the whole school year.
shift.saveFailed: The shift could not be saved

faults.endBeforeStart: The shift must end after it starts.
faults.toBeforeFrom: The end date is before the start date.
faults.noteTooLong: The note can be at most 200 characters.
faults.clash: The teacher is already on duty in {area} on {day} {start}–{end}. A teacher supervises one place at a time.
faults.dateInvalid: Enter a date that exists, or leave the field empty for the school year’s own bound.
faults.noWeekday: No {day} falls between {from} and {to}, so the shift would never run.
faults.fromOutsideYear: The start date must lie within the school year ({from} – {to}).
faults.toOutsideYear: The end date must lie within the school year ({from} – {to}).

errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_CLASH: The teacher already has a shift sharing a minute with this one that day. A teacher supervises one place at a time.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_COVER_CLASH: The teacher covers the break duty in {area} as a substitute on {date}, at the same time as this shift. A supervisor is in one place at a time: undo the decision on the cover board first.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_MOVED: The shift was handed to another teacher since the page was read. Reload the page and try again.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_LIMIT: A school year has at most 2,000 supervision shifts.
errors.SUPERVISION_AREA_NOT_FOUND: The area no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND: The shift no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.SUPERVISION_YEAR_NOT_FOUND: The school year no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.notFound: The teacher, the area or the shift no longer exists. Reload the page.
errors.SUPERVISION_TEACHER_INACTIVE: The teacher is deactivated and cannot be given a shift. Choose another teacher.
errors.SUPERVISION_SHIFT_HAS_COVERS: The cover board has {count, plural, one {a decision} other {# decisions}} on this break duty from {date}. Undo {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} on the cover board first, so the substitute is told.

shift.lessonClashTitle: The shift falls during one of the teacher's lessons
shift.lessonClashSavedTitle: The shift is saved, but it falls during one of the teacher's lessons
shift.lessonClashBody: The generator does not know about supervision shifts yet and may place lessons in the shift's time. Move the shift or the lesson. Also keep the times in the teacher's Break duty, so the generator keeps them free.
shift.inactiveNotice: {name} was deactivated on {date}. The shift covers the break until the day before. If the break needs someone after that, add a shift for another teacher from {date}.
shift.inactiveNoticeNever: {name} was deactivated on {date}, before the shift began, so the shift covers nothing.

teachers.title: Teachers' supervision
teachers.description: The shifts' minutes per week beside the budget in the teacher's Break duty. Shifts count as duties in staffing, and the Break duty counts only in weeks the teacher has no shift.
teachers.caption: Every teacher with shifts or the Break duty this school year
teachers.empty: No teacher has shifts or the Break duty this school year.

teacherWorkTime.title: Working time for {name}
teacherWorkTime.hardRuleHint: Lunch, daily rest and the daily cap are hard requirements: the solver refuses the whole week if it cannot fit them, and names the teacher's row that did not work out. The preferred day off is a wish, not a requirement.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesHint: Unbroken minutes of lunch the teacher is owed. Leave empty if no lunch rule applies.
teacherWorkTime.windowHint: Lunch must both start and end inside the window. The length and the two times belong together — either all three, or none of them.
teacherWorkTime.restMinutesHint: At least this long between the last lesson of one day and the first of the next.
teacherWorkTime.dayCapMinutes: Most minutes of teaching per day
teacherWorkTime.dayCapHint: Every lesson the teacher is on, as teacher or co-teacher, counts from start to end, and overlapping lessons count once. Duties and break supervision do not count. Leave empty if no cap applies.
teacherWorkTime.freeDayHint: A wish, not a rule: the solver tries to leave the teacher the day without lessons, but would rather place lessons there than refuse the week, and says after the run if the wish could not be kept. For part of a day, use Prefer free under Availability.
teacherWorkTime.emptyMeansNoRule: All fields empty means no working-time rule applies to this teacher. A suggestion is not stored until you press Save.
teacherWorkTime.useSuggestion: Use the suggestion: 30 min between 10:30 and 13:30, and 11 hours of rest
teacherWorkTime.cleared: The working-time rule has been removed.
teacherWorkTime.noRule: No working-time rule. The solver promises this teacher neither lunch nor rest, and sets no cap on their teaching per day.
teacherWorkTime.summaryRestHours: At least {hours} hours of rest between two days
teacherWorkTime.summaryRestHoursMinutes: At least {hours} h {minutes} min of rest between two days
teacherWorkTime.summaryDayCap: At most {minutes} min of teaching per day
teacherWorkTime.summaryFreeDay: Wishes to be free on {day, select, 1 {Mondays} 2 {Tuesdays} 3 {Wednesdays} 4 {Thursdays} 5 {Fridays} 6 {Saturdays} 7 {Sundays} other {day {day}}}
teacherWorkTime.lunchTrioIncomplete: The length of lunch and its window belong together. Fill in all three fields, or empty all three.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesOutOfRange: Lunch is given in whole minutes, between {min} and {max}.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesOffGrid: Lunch must be a whole multiple of {step} minutes — the solver's grid is {step} minutes.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowBackwards: The end of the window must fall after its start.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowTooNarrow: The window is {window} minutes wide and does not hold a lunch of {minutes} minutes.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowOffGrid: The window's times must fall on whole {step}-minute intervals, for example 10:30 or 10:35.
teacherWorkTime.restOutOfRange: Daily rest is given in whole minutes, between {min} and {max}.
teacherWorkTime.dayCapOutOfRange: The cap is given in whole minutes, between {min} and {max}.
teacherWorkTime.dayCapOffGrid: The cap must be a whole multiple of {step} minutes — the solver's grid is {step} minutes.
teacherWorkTime.freeDayOutOfRange: Choose a weekday, or No preference.

staffing.title: Staffing
staffing.subtitle: Who teaches how many minutes a week, in which subjects and against which target
staffing.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.
staffing.empty: No teachers with a post or a curriculum entry for this year. Enter posts on the teachers' rows under People, or assign teachers on the curriculum entries.
staffing.loadFailed: The report could not be fetched
staffing.loadFailedHint: No figures are shown, because they would read zero for the wrong reason. Switch the year in the picker above to try again.
staffing.noTargetBody: The school has not chosen a full-time teaching target, so no teacher can be compared against a goal and every row reads No target. The agreement states no weekly measure — the target is the school's own decision.
staffing.kpiUnqualifiedNotRecordedHint: The list is empty because the school has recorded no qualifications at all — not because everyone is qualified.
staffing.weekHintStandard: The standard week weighs a whole-year entry 1, alternate weeks 0.5 and a dated entry by its share of the year's teaching weeks, holidays deducted. The subject columns always show the standard week.
staffing.weekHintPeak: The peak week is the single heaviest ISO week — where a term course and a year course collide although neither is heavy alone. The Teaching and Duties columns each show their own peak week, where a dated duty counts all its minutes in the weeks it runs; the subject columns show the standard week.
staffing.unitHintPercent: Percent of employment is the employment percentage × the subject's share of the teacher's teaching — Statistics Sweden's share of post per subject. Empty for a teacher without a post.
staffing.tableCaption: Staffing per teacher and subject. Cells are minutes per standard week or percent of employment; the last columns are employment, target, teaching, duties, balance and share of target. Teachers over target come first.
staffing.drawerUnqualified: {count, plural, one {# assignment without qualification} other {# assignments without qualification}}
staffing.periodsHint: Change the post from a date, for example 80 % from 1 November. The target is counted week by week: a week belongs to the post in force on its Monday.
staffing.noPeriods: The post is the same all school year.
staffing.periodsTimeline: The post over the school year
staffing.removePeriodBody: The days the period covers get the post's own figures again.
staffing.periodNoWeek: Covers no whole week and changes no target.
staffing.periodPercentSteps: The post's percentage changes during the school year: {steps}
staffing.drawerPeriodsIntro: The post changes during the school year. Each period is held to its own target, and the status above is the worst period.
staffing.periodToHint: Leave empty for the last day of the school year.
staffing.problem_periodFromRequired: Enter the date the period starts.
staffing.problem_periodOutsideYear: {date} is outside the school year ({start} to {end}).
staffing.problem_periodDatesReversed: The period cannot end ({to}) before it starts ({from}).
staffing.problem_periodHoldsNoWeek: The period {from} – {to} contains no Monday. The target is counted week by week, so a period needs at least one whole week.
staffing.problem_periodOverlaps: The period overlaps another period of the post ({from} – {to}). A day has one post.
staffing.employmentHint: The post applies to {year}. The whole row is rewritten when you save.
staffing.signatureHint: At most eight characters, unique per year.
staffing.scbFieldsHint: Goes to SCB's Pedagogisk personal. Fixed-term also covers long-term substitutes and hourly staff. Förstelärare and lektor: how much of the post the career position takes, in whole per cent. Leave empty for a teacher who does not hold it.
staffing.targetOverrideHint: Leave empty to derive the target from the school's full-time figure × (post − reduction), rounded to five minutes. 0 means the post holds no teaching.
staffing.teachingDaysHint: Part-time in days: on how many weekdays the teacher teaches at most. Scheduling holds it as a hard rule. Leave empty for no limit. Shown only to the principal, a full administrator and anyone with HR read.
staffing.derivedNoTarget: Target: no full-time figure set for the school
staffing.derivedRegulated: Regulated working time: {hours} h/year over {days} working days
staffing.noEmployment: No post recorded for this year. The teacher counts without a target until one is saved.
staffing.employmentSummaryTeachingDays: Teaches on at most {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} a week
staffing.qualificationsHint: The whole list is saved at once: what you see is what applies. One subject per row — maths 1–6 and 7–9 is written as 1–9.
staffing.noQualifications: No qualifications recorded. Substitute suggestions and the qualification check fall back to who has a curriculum entry in the subject.
staffing.unstaffedHint: Curriculum entries without a teacher. Suggest teachers ranks the school's teachers by qualification, whether they already teach the group and how much room they have left — one click assigns.
staffing.unstaffedEmpty: Every curriculum entry has a teacher.
staffing.unstaffedShareRow: {group} · {subject} · {lessons, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}} of {length} min without a teacher · {minutes} min/wk
staffing.policyHint: One row for the school. The target decides what each teacher is compared with; the checks decide what happens when a teacher is put on a curriculum entry.
staffing.riktmarkeSource: 1 080 min/wk (630 h/year) is Vimmerby municipality's full-time target in its staffing principles; the Sveriges Lärare survey shows a full-time median of 1 090 min/wk (P10 850, P90 1 280). The agreement (Bilaga M) states no weekly teaching measure, so the figure is the school's own decision.
staffing.toleranceHint: How many percent over target a teacher may be before the row reads Over target.
staffing.modelHint: Minutes: a teacher's load is their lesson minutes. Factor: load = lesson time × the subject's factor (the school's setting per subject). The pupils' lesson minutes are not affected.
staffing.refuseHint: Refuse means an assignment that breaks the check is not saved, with a sentence saying why. Warn saves and shows the sentence. A substitute is always warned, never refused.
staffing.candidateOverAfter: {minutes} min/wk over target with this row
staffing.candidateHint: Qualification and remaining minutes per teacher, from the staffing. The school's settings decide whether an assignment is warned about or refused when it is saved.
staffing.problem_percentRequired: Enter the employment percentage. A post without a percentage is no post.
staffing.problem_percentOutOfRange: The employment percentage is above 0 and at most 100, with at most {decimals} decimals.
staffing.problem_reductionOutOfRange: The reduction is a percentage between 0 and 100, with at most {decimals} decimals.
staffing.problem_reductionAbovePercent: The reduction ({reduction} %) cannot exceed the post ({percent} %).
staffing.problem_targetOutOfRange: The own target is whole minutes per week, at most {max}.
staffing.problem_signatureTooLong: The signature is at most {max} characters.
staffing.problem_noteTooLong: The note is at most {max} characters.
staffing.problem_firstTeacherOutOfRange: The förstelärare share is whole per cent, 1 to 100. Leave the field empty for a teacher who is not a förstelärare.
staffing.problem_lecturerOutOfRange: The lektor share is whole per cent, 1 to 100. Leave the field empty for a teacher who is not a lektor.
staffing.problem_careerAbovePost: Förstelärare ({first} %) and lektor ({lecturer} %) together can be at most the whole post.
staffing.problem_teachingDaysOutOfRange: Teaching days per week is a whole number between {min} and {max}, or left empty for no limit.
staffing.problem_spanReversed: Row {row}: the highest grade ({max}) cannot be below the lowest ({min}). A span is written 7–9, not 9–7.
staffing.problem_validityReversed: Row {row}: the end date is before the start date.
staffing.problem_duplicateSubject: Row {row} has the same subject as row {first}. One qualification per subject — write the span as one.
staffing.problem_riktmarkeOutOfRange: The target is whole minutes per week, between 1 and {max}. Leave it empty for no comparison.
staffing.problem_regulatedOutOfRange: Regulated working time is whole hours per year, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_annualOutOfRange: Annual working time is whole hours per year, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_regulatedAboveAnnual: Regulated working time ({regulated} h) does not fit in the annual working time ({annual} h).
staffing.problem_workDaysOutOfRange: Working days are whole days, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_semesterHoursOutOfRange: The annual-leave contract's weekly hours are above 0 and at most {max}, with at most one decimal.
staffing.problem_toleranceOutOfRange: The tolerance is whole percent between 0 and {max}.
staffing.barCountedDuty: of which {minutes} min duties counted as teaching
staffing.barDuty: {minutes} min other duties, outside the target
staffing.dutyCellCounted: of which {minutes} min count as teaching
staffing.kpiBottlenecksNotComputedHint: Without a single recorded qualification there is no knowing how much room the qualified teachers have left — so no figure, not zero.
staffing.suggestFailed: The suggestions could not be loaded. Close and open again.
staffing.suggestCharge: The row charges its teacher {minutes} min/wk.
staffing.suggestNoQualifications: The school has recorded no qualifications, so the list is ranked by who already teaches the subject or had the group in it last year.
staffing.suggestEmpty: The school has no active teachers to suggest.
staffing.suggestWouldExceed: Over the limit with this row
staffing.suggestUnassign: Remove the teacher from the row
staffing.bottlenecksHint: Per subject: the minutes the unstaffed rows would charge a teacher, against what the teachers qualified in the subject have left to their targets. Short means the rows cannot be staffed without someone going over target.
staffing.bottlenecksNotComputed: No qualifications recorded, so the qualified teachers' capacity cannot be computed. Record qualifications on the teachers' rows and the bottlenecks appear here.
staffing.bottlenecksEmpty: No unstaffed rows, so no demand to compare.
staffing.bottlenecksCaption: Subject bottlenecks: demand from unstaffed rows against the qualified teachers' remaining minutes, shortages first.
staffing.bottleneckRows: {count, plural, one {# unstaffed row} other {# unstaffed rows}}
staffing.dutiesHint: Other duties in {year}: mentoring, subject lead, staff meetings, break duty. A duty can run for part of the year and block fixed times in the timetable.
staffing.dutiesLoadFailed: The duties could not be loaded.
staffing.noDuties: No duties recorded for the year.

problems.ROLLOVER_UNKNOWN_GROUP: A chosen group no longer exists in the year. Reload the page.
problems.ROLLOVER_UNKNOWN_BREAK: A chosen holiday no longer exists in the year. Reload the page.

problems.DUTY_SLOTS_NOT_CARRIED: Duties are not carried over: {duties, plural, one {# duty} other {# duties}}, {blockedSlots, plural, one {# blocked slot} other {# blocked slots}} and {mentorskap, plural, one {# mentorship} other {# mentorships}}. problems.STAFFING_DUTY_GROUP_DROPPED: {duties, plural, one {# duty is} other {# duties are}} carried over without its group, because the group does not exist next year: {groups}.
problems.STAFFING_TEACHERS_NOT_CARRIED: {teachers, plural, one {# person is} other {# people are}} not an active teacher or school leader, so their post and duties are not carried over.
problems.STAFFING_SLOT_OFF_GRID: {duties, plural, one {# duty has} other {# duties have}} a blocked slot off the schedule's grid. The duty is carried over, the slot is not.
problems.STAFFING_PER_YEAR_TERMS_CARRIED: {reductions, plural, =0 {} one {The reduction is carried over for # teacher. } other {The reduction is carried over for # teachers. }}{overrides, plural, =0 {} one {An own target is carried over for # teacher. } other {An own target is carried over for # teachers. }}{dayLimits, plural, =0 {} one {The limit on teaching days per week is carried over for # teacher. } other {The limit on teaching days per week is carried over for # teachers. }}Such terms are often agreed for one year — check that they still apply next year.
problems.STAFFING_SIGNATURE_TAKEN: {teachers, plural, one {# teacher's signature is} other {# teachers' signatures are}} already used by someone else in the year and not carried over.
problems.STAFFING_ALREADY_PRESENT: {teachers, plural, =0 {} one {# teacher already has a post in the year and is skipped whole. } other {# teachers already have a post in the year and are skipped whole. }}{duties, plural, =0 {} one {# duty is not carried over, because it already exists in the year or belongs to a teacher who already has a post there.} other {# duties are not carried over, because they already exist in the year or belong to a teacher who already has a post there.}}
problems.STAFFING_SLOTS_OVER_LESSONS: {duties, plural, one {# blocked slot lands} other {# blocked slots land}} on {lessons, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}} the teacher already has in the year's schedule. They become conflicts to resolve in the schedule.
problems.STAFFING_DUTY_ENDED: {duties, plural, one {# duty ended before the year did and is not carried} other {# duties ended before the year did and are not carried}}, such as a mentorship handed over at Christmas. They are listed under Posts and duties.
problems.STAFFING_DUTY_FROM_CLEARED: {duties, plural, one {# duty started during the year and is carried without its date, so it runs} other {# duties started during the year and are carried without their dates, so they run}} the whole next year. Change the date afterwards if it should start later again.
problems.STAFFING_POST_FROM_PERIOD: {teachers, plural, one {# post changed} other {# posts changed}} during the school year with a period that runs to its last day. Next year gets the post as the period gives it. The teacher is listed under Posts and duties.
problems.STAFFING_POST_PERIODS_ENDED: {teachers, plural, one {# post had} other {# posts had}} periods that ended before the last day of the school year. They are not carried, and next year gets the post as it stands on the teacher's card.
problems.VOLUME_DIFFERS_FROM_TIMPLAN: The teaching requirements of {groups} differ from the decided timplan for the grade they are promoted into.
problems.ROLLOVER_TIMPLAN_CARRIED_MISFIT: Grade {grades} follows {plans} next year, as its cohort does this year, but that plan's wording does not apply to the cohort: the 2028 wording applies to exactly the cohorts starting grade 1 in autumn 2028 or later. Choose another plan under Timplan per year once the year is created.
problems.ROLLOVER_TIMPLAN_NO_FITTING_PLAN: Grade {grades} gets no timplan next year, because no decided plan applies to that cohort. From autumn 2028 the new grade 1 follows only a plan under the 2028 law, and everyone already in school only an older one. Choose a plan under Timplan per year once the year is created.
problems.ISO_WEEK_53_CROSSED: The rollover crosses a week 53: {rows, plural, one {# odd- or even-week requirement switches} other {# odd- or even-week requirements switch}} to the other week type. Check them.
problems.ROLLOVER_2028_RENUMBERING: The new year starts in {startYear} and uses the ten-year numbering: under {source}, every class moves up two grades instead of one (8A becomes 10A, the preschool class starts directly in grade 2), and a class that stays moves up one. A new intake class opens one grade above the lowest class, so the preschool class's becomes the new grade 1; otherwise the new grade 1 is added once the year is created. Every older cohort keeps its timplan and the older total time.
problems.ROLLOVER_2028_NOT_RENUMBERED: The new year starts in {startYear} but keeps the school’s numbering, because the school has none of the school forms {source} renumbers. Classes move up one grade as usual.
problems.ROLLOVER_2028_SCHOOL_FORM_UNKNOWN: The new year starts in {startYear}, when {source} renumbers grundskolan, anpassade grundskolan, specialskolan and sameskolan. Choose the numbering under Grade numbering from autumn 2028.
problems.ROLLOVER_2028_RENUMBERING_REQUIRED: The school has a decided local timplan or a preschool class, so it has one of the school forms {source} renumbers from {startYear}. The numbering cannot be kept.
problems.ROLLOVER_GRADE_ABOVE_12: {groups} would end up above grade 12 next year. Choose another outcome for them.

engineMessages.CONFLICT_CORE_SUMMARY: No timetable satisfies every rule. Start with the causes listed below: together they are enough to make the week impossible, but the solver reports a sufficient set rather than the smallest one, so some of them may carry no blame.
engineMessages.CONFLICT_NO_CORE: No timetable satisfies every rule, and the solver could not name which of them collide.
engineMessages.CONFLICT_NO_CORE_GUESS: Total teaching demand likely exceeds available room or teacher time. Review lessons per week, unavailable windows, and room capacity.
engineMessages.DEMAND_CLIQUE_HOURS_SHORT: Too many lessons for the hours: student group {group} and the {sharingGroups, plural, one {# other group} other {# other groups}} sharing its pupils may never overlap, and between them need {demandMinutes} minutes of lessons a week, but the frame times{lunch, select, none { and the locked lessons} other {, the locked lessons and the lunch}} leave at most {capacityMinutes}. engineMessages.DEMAND_REQUIREMENTS_EXCEED_WEEK: Lessons of {requirements, plural, one {# requirement} other {# requirements}} need {demandMinutes} minutes a week and the week offers {capacityMinutes}.
engineMessages.DEMAND_TEACHER_HOURS_SHORT: Too many lessons for {teachers, plural, one {one teacher's hours} other {the hours of # teachers}}: a teacher gives one lesson at a time, and the lessons named here need more of the week than the school day, the frame times, the rasts, the margins around the lessons and the teacher's locked lessons leave them. engineMessages.DEMAND_TEACHER_LESSONS_EXCEED_ROOM: One teacher gives the lessons of {requirements, plural, one {# requirement} other {# requirements}}, and they need {demandMinutes} minutes a week. engineMessages.GROUP_DAILY_MAXIMUM_CANNOT_BE_KEPT: The school rules allow at most {maxPerDay, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}} a day for each class and teaching group. {measured, select, 1 {That maximum is what makes the week impossible: without it, a timetable exists that keeps every other rule, and in it the groups named here have more lessons than that on some day.} 2 {That maximum makes the week impossible on its own: even with the other rules set aside, the groups named here cannot fit their lessons into the days open to them at that maximum. engineMessages.FRAME_NO_WINDOW_FOR_REQUIREMENT: The frame times leave no room for requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}): its {minutes}-minute lessons need a window, and the widest any day still offers is {remaining} minutes.
engineMessages.MARGIN_NO_WINDOW_FOR_REQUIREMENT: The time around the lessons of requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}) leaves them no day to run on: its {minutes}-minute lessons take {before} minutes before and {after} minutes after for the pupils, {changeover, select, 0 {with no changeover between lessons} other {plus {changeover} minutes of changeover between lessons}}, and the widest any day then leaves for the lesson itself is {remaining} minutes. Shorten the lessons, shorten those margins, or widen the window they all have to fit inside.
engineMessages.INPUT_CONSTRAINT_TIME_OFF_GRID: The constraint on {kind, select, TEACHER {a teacher} ROOM {room {resource}} STUDENT_GROUP {class {resource}} other {years {grades}}} runs {start}-{end}, which does not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid or falls outside the school day.
engineMessages.INPUT_LESSON_LENGTH_OFF_GRID: Requirement {requirement} asks for {minutes}-minute lessons, which do not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid. Use a whole multiple of {slotMinutes} minutes.
engineMessages.INPUT_LESSON_LONGER_THAN_DAY: Requirement {requirement} asks for {minutes}-minute lessons, which are longer than the school day.
engineMessages.INPUT_MODEL_TOO_LARGE: This week is too large to build: about {variables} model variables against a limit of {limit}. The usual causes are rooms with many different capacities, constraints that each touch many lessons, and very high per-teacher lesson loads.
engineMessages.ROOM_MODEL_TOO_LARGE: There are too many rooms to re-deal in one go: about {variables} model variables against a limit of {limit}. The model grows with how many lessons may move and how many rooms each may use. Lock the lessons whose room is settled (a locked lesson keeps both its time and its room), or give subjects room rules that narrow where they may go, and try again.
engineMessages.INPUT_NO_REQUIREMENTS: The timplan is empty: there is nothing to place. Add at least one row.
engineMessages.INPUT_NO_ROOMS: No rooms are registered, so no lesson can be given one.
engineMessages.INPUT_DUPLICATE_REQUIREMENT_ID: Requirement {requirement} appears more than once in the week sent. Every requirement needs an id of its own.
engineMessages.INPUT_TOO_MANY_LESSONS: The week holds {lessons} lessons, more than the {limit} this engine will place in one run. Split the run, or reduce lessons per week.
